Tool.title: Tool
Tool.description: Represents a tool available on pypapers.in, such as calculators, converters, or other utilities.

description.description: Brief description of the tool's functionality.

url.description: URL where the tool can be accessed.

imageUrl.description: URL of the image representing the tool.

Book.title: Book
Book.description: Represents a book available on pypapers.in.

imageUrl.description: URL of the book's cover image.

Audiobook.title: Audiobook
Audiobook.description: Represents an audiobook available on pypapers.in.

audioUrl.description: URL where the audiobook can be streamed or downloaded.

imageUrl.description: URL of the audiobook's cover image.

Note.title: Note
Note.description: Represents a user-created note within the pypapers.in application.

userId.description: Reference to User. (Relationship: User 1:N Note).  Unique identifier of the user who created the note.

content.description: Content of the note (e.g., text, code snippet).

createdAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the note was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the note was last updated.

User.title: User
User.description: Represents a user of the pypapers.in application.

profileImageUrl.description: URL of the user's profile image.

Recommendation.title: Recommendation
Recommendation.description: Represents an AI-generated content recommendation for a user.

userId.description: Reference to User. (Relationship: User 1:N Recommendation).  Unique identifier of the user the recommendation is for.

contentId.description: Identifier of the specific content item being recommended. References Tool.id, Book.id, or Audiobook.id based on contentType.

reason.description: Explanation or reason for the recommendation generated by the AI.

timestamp.description: Timestamp of when the recommendation was generated.

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore structure is designed to provide a secure and scalable solution for the pypapers.in application, focusing on authorization independence and clear security rules. It leverages path-based ownership and denormalization to avoid complex `get()` calls in security rules, which ensures atomic operations and simplifies debugging.

*   **Users Collection:** Stores user profiles.
*   **Tools Collection:** Stores information about the tools available on the platform.  This collection is publicly readable. No write access from users.
*   **Books Collection:** Stores information about the books available on the platform. This collection is publicly readable. No write access from users.
*   **Audiobooks Collection:** Stores information about the audiobooks available on the platform. This collection is publicly readable. No write access from users.
*   **User Notes:** Each user has a dedicated collection for their notes (`/users/{userId}/notes/{noteId}`). This enforces path-based ownership, making security rules straightforward. Only the user can access their own notes.
*   **Recommendations:** Each user has a dedicated collection for recommendations (`/users/{userId}/recommendations/{recommendationId}`). This supports the display of AI recommendations based on the user's interest or past activity. Only the user can access their own recommendations.

This structure promotes Authorization Independence by avoiding the need to fetch parent document data to validate child document access. The design also supports clear QAPs by segregating data based on ownership and access requirements. Publicly available content (tools, books, audiobooks) are stored in root collections without ownership restrictions. User-specific data (notes, recommendations) are stored in subcollections under the user's document.
